bill.name: Stronger Start for Working Families Act
bill.status: Introduced 2026-01-08; read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance

provisions.title: Earned income threshold for the refundable Child Tax Credit
provisions.heading: SEC. 2. EARNED INCOME THRESHOLD FOR REFUNDABLE CHILD TAX CREDIT
provisions.quote: Section 24(d)(1)(B)(i) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “$3,000” and inserting “$1”. (b) CONFORMING AMENDMENT.—Section 24(h) is amended by striking paragraph (6). (c) EFFECTIVE DATE.—… taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
goals: Let the refundable Child Tax Credit phase in from the first dollar of earnings
Extend the full CTC to low-earning working families currently excluded by the $2,500 earnings threshold

effects.mechanism: Refundable CTC (ACTC) earned-income phase-in threshold: $2,500 (current law) -> $1 (statute; PolicyEngine models $0)
effects.text: About 3.5 million working families with children gain; the refundable credit begins phasing in at 15% from the first dollar of earnings instead of above $2,500. Maximum household gain is modest (~$375) and concentrated in the lowest income deciles.

barriers.text: Referred to Finance with no markup scheduled; would need to be reported or folded into a larger tax vehicle. Bipartisan sponsorship (Hassan D + Young R) raises the odds relative to a single-party marker bill, but there is no scheduled vehicle.
Adds ~$1.6B/yr (~$14.6B/10yr, PolicyEngine) of unoffset refundable outlays; any pay-for fight is the live risk to enactment.

metrics.text: SPM child poverty rate (the provision targets low-earning families with children)
Additional Child Tax Credit (refundable ACTC) outlays

conditionals: If S.3596 is enacted, gov.irs.credits.ctc.refundable.phase_in.threshold = $1 for tax years beginning after 2025-12-31 (PolicyEngine policy 85587 models the threshold at $0).

compute.result_summary: 2026: federal budgetary impact -$1.83B (income_tax delta minus benefits delta, measured 0; state spillover -$0.3M reported separately); child poverty -1.2%; 6.5% gain; Gini -0.02%.
